entities.name: Friedrich Graf Kleist von Nollendorf
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Friedrich Emil Ferdinand Heinrich von Kleist, later Graf Kleist von Nollendorf, emerged as a pivotal Prussian field marshal during the tumultuous Napoleonic Wars, particularly distinguished by his command at the Battle of Kulm in August 1813. A scion of the ancient Junker family von Kleist, his military career spanned the critical period of Prussian resurgence following the defeats of Jena-Auerstedt, contributing significantly to the Sixth Coalition's ultimate victory over Napoleon. His strategic acumen and steadfastness in the face of superior French forces solidified his reputation as a formidable commander and a symbol of Prussian military resilience.

Kleist's career began in the Prussian army in 1778, and he steadily rose through the ranks, participating in the Rhine Campaigns of 1793-1794. However, it was during the Wars of Liberation that he achieved his greatest renown. At the Battle of Kulm, he executed a crucial flanking maneuver, arriving from the rear to cut off and decisively defeat the French corps under General Vandamme, preventing the encirclement of a large Allied force and capturing over 10,000 prisoners. This victory, coupled with his participation in the Battle of Leipzig (1813) and the campaign in France (1814), earned him the title Graf Kleist von Nollendorf from King Frederick William III in 1814, commemorating his signal achievement.

His leadership at Kulm not only secured a vital victory but also bolstered the morale of the Allied forces and underscored the effectiveness of combined operations against the French Empire. Kleist's actions contributed to the narrative of Prussian military revival and national pride, which would later become a foundational element of German unification in the latter half of the 19th century. His legacy is enshrined in the annals of Prussian military history as a commander who, through decisive action, helped turn the tide against Napoleonic dominance in Central Europe.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Friedrich Graf Kleist von Nollendorf's crucial role at the Battle of Kulm in 1813 prevented the encirclement of Allied forces and contributed significantly to the eventual defeat of Napoleon in the Sixth Coalition. He solidified the professional reputation of the Prussian military during a critical period of national reassertion.
